1	import ReachyKit

3	/// Keeping the robot's Hugging Face session alive, because nothing on the robot
4	/// can: the daemon stores only the access half of the OAuth token and searches the
5	/// Hub with it. Once that expires the search collapses to `[]` — the daemon catches
6	/// the 401 — and the catalogue quietly loses everything but the curated handful.
7	extension AppStoreModel {
8	    /// Puts a live Hugging Face token back on the robot, and answers whether it had
9	    /// to — a catalogue read behind an expired token is stale.
10	    ///
11	    /// The daemon keeps only the access half and cannot renew it, so this app is the
12	    /// only party that can. A robot that cannot answer at all is left alone:
13	    /// unreachable is not signed out. The outcome is read back from the session's
14	    /// own cache rather than from `linkRobot`, which throws when the relay half
15	    /// fails — by then the token is saved and the account is known.
16	    func relinkHuggingFace(session: RobotSession, token: @MainActor () async -> String?) async -> Bool {
17	        guard session.canLinkHuggingFace, let status = try? await session.robotHFAccount() else { return false }
18	        guard !status.isLoggedIn else {
19	            discoverNeedsHFSignIn = false
20	            return false
21	        }
22	        guard let token = await token() else {
23	            discoverNeedsHFSignIn = true
24	            return false
25	        }
26	        _ = try? await session.linkRobot(token: token)
27	        let linked = await (try? session.robotHFAccount())?.isLoggedIn == true
28	        discoverNeedsHFSignIn = !linked
29	        return linked
30	    }
31	}

findings.explanation: Before this change the only path that copied the user's Hugging Face bearer token to a robot was HFAccountSection.link(), driven by an explicit "Link this robot" tap after a footer that warns "Linking copies your token to the robot over the local network, which is not encrypted. Do it on a network you trust." (RobotSession+HFAuth.swift documents "Two custody points, deliberately" for this reason.) After this change, AppStoreScreen.reload -> AppStoreModel.load -> relinkHuggingFace calls session.linkRobot(token:) automatically on every Apps-tab visit whenever (a) this app has a signed-in HF session (hfAccount.currentToken() returns non-nil) and (b) the connected robot reports isLoggedIn=false — including robots that were never linked before, not only ones whose token expired. The transfer happens over the LAN's plain HTTP saveTokenApiHfAuthSaveTokenPost endpoint (RobotConnection+HFAuth.swift) with no UI confirmation, no warning about the untrusted transport, and no way for the user to decline. A user who is signed in to Hugging Face on this app and connects to any Reachy on the current LAN — a friend's device, a store demo, a colleague's unit, or an attacker-controlled daemon impersonating a Reachy on a hostile network — has their full HF access token silently written to that daemon (and, via refreshRelay, exposed to the relay) simply by opening the Apps tab. This collapses the two custody points into one automatic push and defeats the pre-existing consent+warning control.
findings.fix: Do not call session.linkRobot from load(). Instead, when relinkHuggingFace detects an expired/absent robot HF session, leave discoverNeedsHFSignIn=true and let signInGate direct the user to the Settings flow (or a purpose-built confirmation sheet) that already surfaces the plain-HTTP warning and requires an explicit tap. If the auto-relink is kept, gate it behind a per-robot "remember consent to relink" flag that is only set after the user acknowledges the LAN warning at least once for that robot's hardwareID.
